title: Implement incident-aware burn cooling with synthetic-load safety and tiered paging windows
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: Over the last two capacity incidents (2025-09 and 2025-10) we observed short, high-amplitude burn spikes that triggered multiple pages even when the underlying issue was transient and self-healing (autoscaler oscillation + cold-kernel thrash). Current burn-rate paging thresholds are binary and insensitive to context, leading to noisy on-call churn and wasted mitigation effort.

Goal: Reduce actionable pager volume by introducing an incident-aware burn cooling subsystem that: 1) applies short-term dampening when a verified incident or known autoscaler oscillation is in flight; 2) performs a synthetic-load safety check before suppressing pages (to avoid masking real regressions); and 3) replaces a single hard threshold with tiered paging windows and graduated escalation (informational -> on-call page). This work must preserve detection of genuine customer-impacting regressions and maintain compliance with existing SLA commitments.
acceptance_criteria: Pager count from burn-rate alerts decreases by >=50% in the first 30 minutes of transient capacity events during pilot windows (measured across two production teams)
No missed high-impact regressions during 6-week canary (validated by retrospective and synthetic-load fail-injections)
Feature toggle and safe-mode rollback path implemented (console toggle + audit log entry)
Runbook updates published and linked; on-call docs include decision tree for suppressed alarms
updates: 2025-11-10: Initial design review with SREs and on-call leads; consensus on three components: detection, cooling policy, synthetic safety probe
2025-11-17: Prototype cooling service v0.1 implemented as sidecar to alert-evaluator; added in-memory short-term state for decay hysteresis (PR #4281)

2025-11-22: Integration test injected autoscaler oscillation in staging; cooling suppressed 78% of pages while synthetic probe caught a real throughput regression and allowed one critical page through
2025-11-27: Security & compliance consult — synthetic probe results will be logged to encrypted audit stream (KMS-protected); security_review_required set to true
2025-12-01: Rolling canary started for telemetry and payments teams (2-hour windows daily); early telemetry shows 48% reduction in redundant pages during cool-down windows
comments: Alex (SRE): We should ensure the synthetic probe uses same path as customer-critical RPCs; avoid cheap probes that give false safety signals.
Priya (PM): Add dashboard panels for suppressed pages and synthetic-probe failure rate; product teams want visibility before full rollout.
Rafael (assignee): Plan to add a panic-key in console to disable cooling with one-click during incidents. Will raise PR for UI change.
Maya (creator): Link to related postmortem: GH-ops/incident-2025-09-capacity-regression.md — lessons learned used in design decisions
